title: Why Data Loading Matters 📥
description: Understand the need for efficient data pipelines and the Dataset/DataLoader duo.

slides.title: The Conveyor Belt Analogy 🏭
slides.content:
# Feeding the Model

Training a neural network requires **data** — often millions of samples. We can't load everything into memory at once, nor feed one sample at a time.

PyTorch provides two core abstractions:
* **`Dataset`** – the warehouse of samples.
* **`DataLoader`** – the conveyor belt that delivers batches.

They work together to make data feeding efficient and shuffle-able.

quizData.question: What is the main purpose of a DataLoader?

options.text: To load the entire dataset into GPU memory
To iterate over batches of data efficiently

quizData.explanation: DataLoader handles batching, shuffling, and multi-processing to feed data to the model.

slides.title: Why Not Just a Big Tensor? 🤔
slides.content:
## Memory Constraints

If your dataset is 100K images of size 256x256, loading them all at once would consume ~25 GB of RAM. With DataLoader:
* Only a few batches are in memory at any time.
* Multi-worker loading keeps the GPU busy while data is prepared.
* Shuffling is easy and reproducible.

slides.title: Minimal DataLoader Example
slides.content: Wrap a simple tensor dataset in a DataLoader.
slides.codeSnippet:
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset

data = torch.randn(100, 3, 32, 32)   # 100 images
targets = torch.randint(0, 10, (100,))
dataset = TensorDataset(data, targets)
loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=16, shuffle=True)

for batch_x, batch_y in loader:
    print(batch_x.shape, batch_y.shape)
    break

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always Shuffle Training Data

Set `shuffle=True` for the training DataLoader to avoid learning order-dependent patterns. For validation, keep `shuffle=False`.
